am.B: ደግሞም፦ «ጌታ የጥበበኞች አሳብ ምን ያህል ባዶ እንደ ሆነ ያውቃል።»
am.R: ሌላ ክፍል ደግሞ እንዲህ ይላል፦ «ጌታ የጥበበኛ ሰዎች አሳብ ዋጋ ቢስ መሆኑን ያውቃል።»

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 94:11
decisions.reason: The words are from Psalm 94:11 (93:11 in the Greek numbering). The psalm says the Lord knows the thoughts of human beings; Paul says "of the wise", applying the verse to his point. Reviewers should check the wording against the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: Lord: in Psalm 94:11 this stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Psalm 94:11 the word is the divine name; the Greek Old Testament and Paul have Κύριος.

decisions.choice: futile: empty, achieving nothing
decisions.reason: μάταιοι describes what has no result or substance. The Greek of Ecclesiastes uses the related noun for what is "vanity", like a breath.

decisions.choice: knows the reasonings, that they are futile: knows that they are futile
decisions.reason: Greek often names the object first and then says what is known about it; the sense is that the Lord knows how futile their reasoning is.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: "The LORD" is kept for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Paul quotes the psalm with the Greek word for "Lord", so English writes "Lord", as in John 1:23; m2 notes the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: another passage says
decisions.reason: Readable says what "again" refers to: a second passage of Scripture.

decisions.choice: "Chúa", not "CHÚA", in this quotation of Psalm 94:11
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, the word Paul quotes; the Hebrew of the psalm has the divine name (m2). As in 2:16 and Romans 11:34.

decisions.choice: "주" (L); "주님" (B, R), with no divine_name span
decisions.reason: The psalm has the divine name; Paul's Greek has "Lord", given as in Romans' quotations.

source.text: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν, εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν, ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So that let no one boast in human beings; for all things of you are, \v 22 whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or [the] world or life or death or things present or things coming, all of you, \v 23 and you of Christ, and Christ of God.

en.L: So let no one boast in human beings; for all things are yours, \v 22 whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or [the] world or life or death or things present or things to come, all [are] yours, \v 23 and you [are] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}'s, and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] God's.
en.B: So let no one take pride in mere human beings. Everything is yours: \v 22 Paul or Apollos or Cephas, the world, life or death, what is here now or what is still to come. It all belongs to you, \v 23 and you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} belongs to God.
en.R: So do not brag about following any human leader. Everything belongs to you. \v 22 Paul, Apollos and Peter all belong to you. The world, life and death, what is happening now and what will happen in the future: all of it is yours. \v 23 And you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} belongs to God.

fr.L: Ainsi, que personne ne se vante d’êtres humains ; car tout est à vous, \v 22 soit Paul, soit Apollos, soit Céphas, soit le monde, soit la vie, soit la mort, soit les choses présentes, soit les choses à venir, tout [est] à vous, \v 23 et vous, [vous êtes] au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} [est] à Dieu.
fr.B: Que personne donc ne tire fierté de simples êtres humains. Tout est à vous : \v 22 Paul, Apollos ou Céphas, le monde, la vie ou la mort, le présent ou l’avenir. Tout vous appartient, \v 23 et vous, vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} appartient à Dieu.
fr.R: Alors, ne vous vantez pas de suivre tel ou tel chef humain. Tout vous appartient. \v 22 Paul, Apollos et Pierre vous appartiennent tous. Le monde, la vie et la mort, ce qui se passe maintenant et ce qui arrivera plus tard : tout est à vous. \v 23 Et vous, vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} appartient à Dieu.

es.L: Así que nadie se gloríe en los seres humanos; porque todo es {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}, \v 22 sea Pablo, sea Apolos, sea Cefas, sea [el] mundo, sea [la] vida, sea [la] muerte, sea lo presente, sea lo por venir, todo [es] {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}, \v 23 y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, y {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} [es] de Dios.
es.B: Así que nadie se sienta orgulloso de simples seres humanos. Todo es {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}: \v 22 Pablo, Apolos o Cefas, el mundo, la vida o la muerte, lo que está aquí ahora o lo que aún ha de venir. Todo {{plural_you:les|os}} pertenece, \v 23 y {{plural_you:ustedes pertenecen|vosotros pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, y {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} pertenece a Dios.
es.R: Así que nadie presuma de seguir a un líder humano. Todo {{plural_you:les|os}} pertenece. \v 22 Pablo, Apolos y Pedro {{plural_you:les|os}} pertenecen. El mundo, la vida y la muerte, lo que pasa ahora y lo que pasará en el futuro: todo es {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}. \v 23 Y {{plural_you:ustedes pertenecen|vosotros pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, y {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} pertenece a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mtu yeyote asijivunie wanadamu; kwa maana yote ni yenu, \v 22 kama ni Paulo, au Apolo, au Kefa, au ulimwengu, au uzima, au mauti, au mambo ya sasa, au mambo yajayo, yote [ni] yenu, \v 23 nanyi [ni] wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [ni] wa Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mtu yeyote asione fahari juu ya wanadamu tu. Kila kitu ni chenu: \v 22 Paulo au Apolo au Kefa, ulimwengu, uzima au kifo, yaliyopo sasa au yatakayokuja. Vyote ni vyenu, \v 23 nanyi ni mali ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mali ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msijigambe kwamba mnamfuata kiongozi fulani wa kibinadamu. Kila kitu ni chenu. \v 22 Paulo, Apolo na Petro wote ni wenu. Ulimwengu, uzima na kifo, yanayotokea sasa na yatakayotokea baadaye: yote ni yenu. \v 23 Nanyi ni mali ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mali ya Mungu.

vi.L: Vậy, đừng ai khoe mình về loài người; vì mọi sự đều thuộc về anh chị em, \v 22 dù là Phao-lô, hay A-bô-lô, hay Sê-pha, hay thế gian, hay sự sống, hay sự chết, hay những điều hiện tại, hay những điều tương lai, mọi sự [đều] thuộc về anh chị em, \v 23 và anh chị em [thuộc] về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, và {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} [thuộc] về Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vậy, đừng ai tự hào về những con người. Mọi sự đều thuộc về anh chị em: \v 22 Phao-lô, A-bô-lô hay Sê-pha, thế gian, sự sống hay sự chết, những gì đang có bây giờ hay những gì sẽ đến. Tất cả đều thuộc về anh chị em, \v 23 còn anh chị em thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, và {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Vậy đừng khoe khoang về việc mình đi theo một người lãnh đạo nào. Mọi sự đều thuộc về anh chị em. \v 22 Phao-lô, A-bô-lô và Phi-e-rơ đều thuộc về anh chị em. Thế gian, sự sống và sự chết, những gì đang xảy ra bây giờ và những gì sẽ xảy ra trong tương lai: tất cả đều là của anh chị em. \v 23 Còn anh chị em thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, và {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러므로 아무도 사람을 자랑하지 마십시오. 모든 것이 여러분의 것이기 때문입니다. \v 22 바울이든 아볼로든 게바든, 세상이든 생명이든 죽음이든, 현재 있는 것들이든 장래의 것들이든, 모든 것이 여러분의 것이고, \v 23 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 것이며, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}는 하나님의 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 아무도 사람을 자랑하지 마십시오. 모든 것이 여러분의 것입니다. \v 22 바울이나 아볼로나 게바나, 세상이나 생명이나 죽음이나, 지금 있는 것이나 앞으로 올 것이나, 모두 여러분의 것입니다. \v 23 그리고 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 속해 있고, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 하나님께 속해 계십니다.
ko.R: 그러니 어떤 지도자를 따른다고 뽐내지 마십시오. 모든 것이 여러분의 것입니다. \v 22 바울도 아볼로도 베드로도 모두 여러분의 것입니다. 세상도, 삶과 죽음도, 지금 일어나는 일과 앞으로 일어날 일도, 모두 여러분의 것입니다. \v 23 그리고 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 속해 있고, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 하나님께 속해 계십니다.

pt.L: Assim, ninguém se glorie em seres humanos; pois todas as coisas são de vocês, \v 22 seja Paulo, seja Apolo, seja Cefas, seja [o] mundo, seja vida, seja morte, sejam coisas presentes, sejam coisas por vir, todas [são] de vocês, \v 23 e vocês [são] {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}}, e {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} [é] de Deus.
pt.B: Por isso, ninguém se orgulhe de meros seres humanos. Tudo pertence a vocês: \v 22 Paulo, Apolo ou Cefas, o mundo, a vida ou a morte, o que existe agora ou o que ainda está por vir. Tudo pertence a vocês, \v 23 e vocês pertencem {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}}, e {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} pertence a Deus.
pt.R: Por isso, não se gabem de seguir este ou aquele líder humano. Tudo pertence a vocês. \v 22 Paulo, Apolo e Pedro pertencem a vocês. O mundo, a vida e a morte, o que está acontecendo agora e o que vai acontecer no futuro: tudo isso é de vocês. \v 23 E vocês pertencem {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}}, e {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} pertence a Deus.

am.L: ስለዚህ ማንም በሰዎች አይመካ፤ ሁሉ የእናንተ ነውና፤ \v 22 ጳውሎስ ቢሆን አጵሎስም ቢሆን ኬፋም ቢሆን፣ ዓለምም ቢሆን ሕይወትም ቢሆን ሞትም ቢሆን፣ ያለውም ቢሆን የሚመጣውም ቢሆን፣ ሁሉ የእናንተ [ነው]፤ \v 23 እናንተም {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} [ናችሁ]፤ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ደግሞ የእግዚአብሔር [ነው]።
am.B: ስለዚህ ማንም በሰዎች አይኩራ። ሁሉ ነገር የእናንተ ነው፤ \v 22 ጳውሎስም ሆነ አጵሎስ ወይም ኬፋ፣ ዓለምም፣ ሕይወትም ሆነ ሞት፣ አሁን ያለውም ሆነ ወደ ፊት የሚመጣው፣ ሁሉም የእናንተ ነው፤ \v 23 እናንተ ደግሞ {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} ናችሁ፤ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ደግሞ የእግዚአብሔር ነው።
am.R: ስለዚህ የትኛውንም ሰብዓዊ መሪ በመከተላችሁ አትኩራሩ። ሁሉ ነገር የእናንተ ነው። \v 22 ጳውሎስ፣ አጵሎስና ጴጥሮስ ሁሉም የእናንተ ናቸው። ዓለም፣ ሕይወትና ሞት፣ አሁን እየሆነ ያለውና ወደ ፊት የሚሆነው፣ ሁሉም የእናንተ ነው። \v 23 እናንተ ደግሞ {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} ናችሁ፤ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ደግሞ የእግዚአብሔር ነው።

decisions.choice: boast in human beings: take pride in human leaders and put confidence in them
decisions.reason: καυχάσθω is to boast or take pride in something. The Corinthians were boasting of the leaders they followed; Paul has already said that the only right boasting is in the Lord (1:31).

decisions.choice: all things are yours: the slogans turned around
decisions.reason: The Corinthians said "I am of Paul" (1:12; 3:4). Paul turns it around: Paul, Apollos and Cephas belong to the church, as servants given for its good.

decisions.choice: Cephas: the Aramaic name, meaning "rock", of the apostle Peter
decisions.reason: Jesus gave Simon this name (John 1:42). Paul usually calls him Cephas (1:12; 9:5; 15:5; Galatians 2:9).

decisions.choice: the world: the created order and everything in it
decisions.reason: In verse 19 the world is the human order with its false wisdom; here, in a list with life and death and the present and the future, it is the whole created world. All of it serves God's people, because they belong to Christ.

decisions.choice: things present and things to come: the present and the future
decisions.reason: ἐνεστῶτα and μέλλοντα are participles, "what is here" and "what is going to be". Romans 8:38 has the same pair.

decisions.choice: Christ belongs to God: as the Son who comes from the Father and does his work
alternatives: Christ is less than God in his nature
decisions.reason: Paul says something similar in 11:3 and 15:28, of the Son's relation to the Father and his work. He also calls Christ the one Lord through whom all things exist (8:6). The point here is the chain of belonging: the church does not belong to its leaders but to Christ, and through Christ to God.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal writes "{{christos:Christ|Messiah}}'s" for the possessive.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Young readers know the apostle as Peter, so Readable uses that name here as it does in 1:12 (m3).

decisions.choice: take pride in mere human beings (B); brag about following any human leader (R)
decisions.reason: "Boast in" is not natural English. Readable says what the boasting was about (m1).

decisions.choice: se vanter (L); tirer fierté (B); se vanter (R)
decisions.reason: As the Corinthians term sheet: Balanced says "take pride" where the argument does not turn on the word itself. Readable's "brag" is French "se vanter", pride that takes credit, so it keeps the Literal word.

decisions.choice: se gloríe (L); se sienta orgulloso (B); presuma (R)
decisions.reason: As recorded at 1:29: Literal keeps "gloriarse" so the word can be traced. Here the argument does not turn on the word itself, so Balanced says "sentirse orgulloso", and Readable "presumir", for pride that takes credit for what is a gift.

decisions.choice: que nadie presuma (third person)
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns to "do not brag". Spanish keeps the Greek "let no one", which is just as plain and needs no plural "you".

decisions.choice: asione fahari juu ya (B); msijigambe (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "kujivunia" (1:29). Here the argument does not turn on the word itself, so Balanced says "kuona fahari" (take pride), as Swahili Romans 15:17 does, and Readable says "kujigamba" (brag), since this is pride that takes credit, as the English Readable says "brag".

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" (L); "tự hào" (B); "khoe khoang" (R)
decisions.reason: The founder's rule for this word family: Literal always keeps "khoe mình"; Balanced says "tự hào" where Paul's argument does not turn on the word; Readable says "khoe khoang" for pride that takes credit, as the English says "brag". These are the words of the Vietnamese Romans and Galatians.

decisions.choice: "자랑하다" (L, B); "뽐내다" (R)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "take pride" and Readable "brag" for pride that takes credit for human leaders. Korean "자랑하다" already covers taking pride, so Balanced keeps it; Readable says "뽐내다" (brag), the word it uses again in 4:7.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}는 하나님의 것입니다" (L), without the honorific, keeping the parallel with "여러분은 ... 것이며"
alternatives: the honorific form "께서는 하나님께 속해 계십니다" in Literal too
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's three matching phrases ("yours ... Christ's ... God's"); Balanced and Readable say "belong to" with the honorific for Christ.

decisions.choice: se glorie (L); se orgulhe (B); se gabem (R)
decisions.reason: Following the rule for boasting set at 1:29: Literal keeps "gloriar-se"; Balanced says "orgulhar-se", as the English says "take pride"; Readable says "gabar-se", the word for bragging, as the English says "brag" for pride that takes credit for leaders who are God's gift.

decisions.choice: አይመካ (L); አይኩራ (take pride, B); አትኩራሩ (brag, R)
alternatives: መመካት at every level, as in 1:29-31
decisions.reason: As the book's terms note sets for the English: Literal keeps "መመካት" so the word can be traced; here Paul's point is pride in human leaders, not the word itself, so Balanced says "መኩራት" and Readable "መኩራራት", bragging.
